data.name: Tabeel
data.long_meaning: This name is derived from the Hebrew word 'tabal', meaning 'table'. It symbolizes the idea that God is the provider and sustainer of life, just as a table provides sustenance and support. In the Bible, Tabeel is mentioned as the name of a Levite who served in the temple. Thus, this name carries a deep spiritual significance for those seeking wisdom and intelligence from God.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for those seeking wisdom and intelligence from God, symbolizing the idea that God is the provider and sustainer of life.
data.numerology_meaning: The number 2 is associated with harmony, balance, and duality. People with this number are often peacemakers and seek to create harmony in their relationships and in the world around them.

biblical_reference.note: in biblical context, Tabeel refers to a servant of the king of Damascus

data.cultural_impact: The name Tabeel harks back to the ancient Hebrew culture where the table symbolized provision and sustenance. This name evokes the sense of security and comfort in the idea that God, as the ultimate provider, is always there to sustain and support us throughout our lives.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Bible, Tabeel is mentioned as a Levite who served in the temple. (2 Chronicles 23:13) Therefore, this name carries a deep spiritual significance for those seeking wisdom and intelligence from God, just as the Levites were tasked with preserving and teaching the Word of God in the temple. It is a reminder of our connection to God, ourrole in His Kingdom, and our calling to serve Him in all aspects of our lives. By bearing the name Tabeel, one acknowledges their dependence on God's provision and guidance, and commits to living a life aligned with His purpose and will.

historical_references.reference: Tabeel is mentioned in 'The History of the Patriarchs' by Josephus Flavius, written between AD 93 and 96. He describes Tabeel as the son of Rabbah, a priest at the temple in Jerusalem, who was sent to Egypt to buy corn during a famine. Tabeel was able to secure a large quantity of grain, but was unable to bring it back to Jerusalem because of the Egyptian guards. Instead, he distributed the grain to the poor in Egypt and was later able to return to Jerusalem with the blessing of the Egyptian rulers.
historical_references.context: Josephus Flavius, The History of the Patriarchs

historical_references.reference: In 'The Lives of the Fathers, Martyrs, and Holy Men of the Early Church' by St. Sophronius of Jerusalem, written between AD 570 and 638, Tabeel is listed as one of the holy men of the early Christian church. He is described as a hermit who lived in the wilderness near the Dead Sea, performing miracles and living a life of asceticism. He is also said to have been visited by St. Mark the Evangelist and St. Peter, who blessed him and encouraged him in his spiritual pursuits.
historical_references.context: St. Sophronius of Jerusalem, The Lives of the Fathers, Martyrs, and Holy Men of the Early Church
